canvas.description: the page ground on every surface: the web app, the waitlist, the extension popup and the emails. The only surface `text-faint` may sit on.

surface-soft.description: a barely lifted band: dividers, tag chips at rest, quiet table stripes.

surface-card.description: the default card and panel: Item cards, inputs, dialogs, the nav pill.

surface-strong.description: emphasised cards, selected tabs and chips, the Cue, toasts, secondary and danger buttons.

hairline.description: decorative 1px edges only. At 1.03 to 1.22:1 it reads as one more elevation step, not as a line a User can find, so it never marks something interactive.

control-border.description: the boundary of anything a User types into or ticks: inputs, checkboxes, radio buttons, fields. 3.03:1 on surface-strong up to 3.6:1 on canvas, so it clears the 3:1 non-text minimum on every surface. It is used only on interactive boundaries.

text-heading.description: headlines, primary text, Item titles and the focus ring. 11.1 to 13.2:1.

text-muted.description: captions, labels and the meta line on cards, and the label of a disabled accent control. 4.8 to 5.7:1, so it is the smallest tier allowed on a card.

text-faint.description: fine print and timestamps, **on canvas only** (4.61:1). On any card it drops below 4.5:1 (3.9 to 4.4:1), so meta on cards uses Taupe instead.

accent.description: the primary action's fill and the resurfacing signal: the logo's rising dot, the lit card's 1px edge and glow, the thread that draws to it, the dot that rises on its corner. As text it is allowed only at display sizes (24px and up) on canvas, where its 3.2:1 passes the large-text rule; on cards it is 2.69 to 3.05:1, so it is never a link, a focus ring, a label or small text.

accent-active.description: hover and press on a filled accent control.

accent-disabled.description: a disabled accent control's fill, the same value as the hairline, with its label in Taupe.

on-accent.description: text and icons on Rust (5.75:1) and Fired Rust (7.95:1).

danger.description: error text, error borders and destructive actions. 4.58:1 on surface-strong up to 5.45:1 on canvas, so error text is readable on every surface.

display-xl.purpose: the waitlist and marketing hero headline only. Never in the app.

display.purpose: page titles, empty states and the wordmark.

body-lead.purpose: the paragraph under a hero headline, capped at about 30em.

body.purpose: running text, field text and dialog copy.

body-sm.purpose: supporting copy, toasts, the Cue, the extension popup.

card-title.purpose: Item titles on cards (clamped to whole lines, never cut mid-word) and button labels.

label.purpose: tags, Item type badges, form labels and table headers. Nothing else.

mono.purpose: source domains, URLs and timestamps in running layouts.

mono-sm.purpose: the meta line on cards ("example.com · saved in March").

hand.purpose: the one handwritten sentence above the waitlist headline. Upright, never italic.

shadows.name: field-rest
shadows.purpose: the waitlist's email field (`input-search`): a faint Parchment top highlight and a drop beneath.

shadows.name: palette
shadows.purpose: floating palettes: the sticky nav pill on the secondary pages, the toast, menus.

shadows.name: window
shadows.purpose: the browser window in the waitlist demo.

shadows.name: cue
shadows.purpose: the Cue, the highest surface on its screen.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: the full-screen layer under a dialog or the detail sheet below 1024px. Flat black, no blur.

shadows.name: lit-glow
shadows.purpose: An Item that has come back. The only coloured light in the system. A 22px blur on phones.

shadows.name: pile-edges
shadows.purpose: a stacked card on the waitlist wall, two card edges peeking out below it. It depicts the pile of Items (the same stack as the logo's bars) and is used only on stacked Item cards.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: The one curve for every transition and entrance: a quick start that settles slowly.

motion.name: duration-150
motion.purpose: Hover and colour changes: a button's fill, a chip's text, an edge brightening.

motion.name: duration-300
motion.purpose: Small state changes: the 0.97 press scale and its release, a chip being selected, a toast or a dialog fading and scaling in from 0.98.

motion.name: duration-600
motion.purpose: Surfaces arriving: the detail panel sliding in, the Cue's fade, the joined card replacing the waitlist form.

motion.name: duration-900
motion.purpose: Resurfacing: a card lighting up, its thread drawing in, its dot rising, the Cue moving into place, the wall fading in, the waitlist's staggered rise on load.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Every button on press, over 300ms on the spring.

motion.name: skeleton-pulse
motion.purpose: A Processing card's skeleton bars, between 60% and 100% opacity.

motion.name: wall-drift
motion.purpose: The card wall drifts a few pixels to and fro. One of the two exceptions to the spring.

motion.name: thread-spark
motion.purpose: A spark runs along a drawn thread. The other exception to the spring.

narrative.overview:
Resonory is drawn as a warm, dark, quiet archive: a pile of the User's own saved Items on a near-black ground the colour of an unlit room, read by lamplight. Text is not white but a family of warm beiges, from a parchment heading down to a faint fine print, so the screen reads like paper in low light rather than a glowing display. Nothing on the screen is loud except the one thing the product exists to do. When an Item comes back, its card lights up in rust, a thread draws to it, and a small dot rises above it, exactly like the dot rising above the stacked bars of the logo. That moment, and the one button that asks the User to act, are the only places the warm rust appears; everything else is held in browns and beiges so it can land.

The system is tonal by construction. Surfaces separate by small, warm steps (canvas, surface-soft, surface-card, surface-strong) rather than by borders, and a 1px hairline is a decorative edge only, never the thing that tells a User where to click or type: interactive boundaries carry their own control border. Type is split by meaning. Spectral, a serif, carries language about what a save means (page titles, section headings, empty states, the wordmark). Work Sans carries the interface. JetBrains Mono carries everything the product records about an Item: when, where from, how much was read.

Density is calm, with air. Motion is slow and springy: one curve, a handful of durations, and a still final state for every animation under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: A warm near-black canvas (#151414) with tonal surface steps; dark only, emails included. There is no light theme.
One beige family for text (#E9D8C4 down to #877E74), every tier at 4.5:1 or better where it is allowed.
One accent, rust (#A8492B), with two meanings only: the primary action's fill, and an Item coming back.
Spectral for meaning, Work Sans for interface, JetBrains Mono for what the machine records, and one handwritten Caveat line above the waitlist headline.
Focus is always a 2px text-heading outline, never rust.
One easing curve (cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)) for every state change.

rules.name: The Rust Means Back or Act Rule
rules.body: Rust has two meanings: the primary action (one filled button per view) and an Item coming back. It is never a link colour, a focus ring, a label, an icon colour or small text. If a new surface wants rust anywhere else, use Parchment instead. Links are Parchment with an underline.

rules.name: The One Beige Family Rule
rules.body: Text comes in five warm tiers, Parchment to Dust, and nothing else. A new level of emphasis picks one of the five; it does not introduce a new grey or an opacity of white.

rules.name: The Errors Are Red Rule
rules.body: Errors and destructive actions are Error Red, and red means nothing else. It never competes with Rust, which still means "act" or "came back".

rules.name: The Borders Are Steps Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by tonal steps first. The hairline is decoration; anything a User acts on carries the Control Edge, and anything focused carries the Parchment ring.

rules.name: The Machine Speaks Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything the product records about an Item (when, where from, how far read, how many) is JetBrains Mono, at mono-sm on cards and mono elsewhere. Sentences a person reads are never mono.

rules.name: The Colour, Not Slant Rule
rules.body: Emphasis inside a headline is colour, not italic: an `em` set upright in Rust, and only inside a display-size headline about saving and bringing back, where Rust text passes the large-text rule.

rules.name: The Label Is Not an Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: The uppercase label style is for tags, Item type badges, form labels and table headers only. It is never placed above a headline as a kicker or eyebrow; headings stand unboxed.

rules.name: The Caveat Once Rule
rules.body: Caveat appears exactly once, in the sentence above the waitlist headline. Nowhere else, in no other surface.

rules.name: The Only Light Is Rust Rule
rules.body: Shadows are black and soft. There are no white glows and no coloured light anywhere except the Rust lit glow on an Item that has come back, and its thread. Focus is an outline, never a glow.

dos: **Do** keep Rust (#A8492B) to two jobs: the view's one primary fill (hover and press #863A22, label #FFFFFF), and an Item coming back (the lit card's 1px edge and `0 0 28px rgb(168 73 43 / 0.45)` glow, its thread, its rising dot, the logo's dot).
**Do** set Rust as text only at 24px and up, on the canvas (#151414): the headline's highlighted verbs and the emails' heading and founder name.
**Do** focus every interactive element with a 2px solid #E9D8C4 outline at a 2px offset.
**Do** give every input, checkbox and field a 1px #736D68 Control Edge, and every error a #D36E6E edge and message.
**Do** set meta on cards in Taupe (#988E81, `mono-sm` 11/16); keep Dust (#877E74) for fine print on the canvas.
**Do** set every timestamp, source domain, URL, count and keycap in JetBrains Mono: 11/16 on cards, 13/20 elsewhere.
**Do** nest rounded elements concentrically: a 14px panel with a 6px inset holds a 10px button.
**Do** use `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)` at 150, 300, 600 or 900ms for every transition; only the wall's drift (44s, `ease-in-out`) and the thread's spark (1.4s, `linear`) differ.
**Do** press buttons to `scale(0.97)` and give every animation a still final state under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
**Do** lay the Library out as `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(240px, 1fr))` with a 16px gap, on the 640, 1024 and 1440px breakpoints.
**Do** set the emails' ground with `bgcolor="#151414"` and `color-scheme: dark`, with Georgia and Arial named as fallbacks.
**Do** use Phosphor icons, regular weight, at 16 or 20px, in `currentColor`.
donts: **Don't** use Rust for a link, a focus ring, a label, an icon, a border on a field, or any text under 24px; on a card it is 2.69 to 3.05:1.
**Don't** set Dust (#877E74) on any card or panel (3.88 to 4.40:1); use Taupe (#988E81).
**Don't** mark an interactive boundary with the hairline (#282624, 1.03 to 1.22:1); it is decoration.
**Don't** signal an error in Rust, or use Error Red (#D36E6E) for anything but errors and destructive actions.
**Don't** put two filled Rust buttons in one view; the second is secondary (#262422 with a #736D68 edge).
**Don't** introduce a new grey, an opacity of white, or a light theme; text is one of the five beige tiers, and the system is dark only.
**Don't** set human-facing sentences in mono, or slant a headline's highlighted words (they are upright Rust).
**Don't** place an uppercase `label` (12/16, 0.04em) above a headline as an eyebrow; it is for tags, Item type badges, form labels and table headers.
**Don't** add white glows, coloured shadows other than the lit glow, or a blurred scrim; the scrim is flat `rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6)`.
**Don't** use photographs on the waitlist wall (its pictures are the sun-over-ridge placeholder), or overlay text and badges on a Library Thumbnail.
**Don't** animate layout properties, or use any easing but the spring outside the two exceptions.
**Don't** use Caveat anywhere but the one sentence above the waitlist headline.
